Plan to spend several days exploring Bonito and its surroundings in Mato Grosso do Sul. Clear rivers, waterfalls and caves combine with snorkeling, rafting, walks and other outdoor activities.


One of the region's most recognizable natural attractions is Blue Lake Cave. At Rio da Prata, the clear water lets you observe aquatic life while snorkeling.


For a more active itinerary, add rafting, trekking, horseback riding or cycling. Bonito pairs naturally with the Pantanal if you want to explore different landscapes and observe wildlife.

Bouza Winery is located near Montevideo. Here you can see the vineyards and learn how wine is produced at a small winery.

The experience continues at the table, where wines are paired with dishes to reveal how their flavors and aromas change. A visit to Bouza fits conveniently into a trip to Uruguay's capital.

Brabant is the second-largest island in the Palmer Archipelago, situated between Anvers Island and Liège Island. It stretches from north to south and has mountainous terrain. Glaciers cover most of its slopes, with rocky peaks rising above them; Mount Parry is the island's highest point.

The island was named during the Belgian Antarctic Expedition of 1897–1899. Its name refers to the Belgian province of Brabant and the people who supported the expedition. Approaching by sea, you can appreciate the island's size through the succession of glacial slopes, dark cliffs and mountain ridges. How close a vessel can approach particular stretches of coastline depends on the conditions of the voyage.

Brasília lies in the heart of Brazil on the Central Plateau. The city was built in the 20th century as the country's new capital and is famous for its modernist architecture and carefully planned layout.

The main reason to visit is its modern architecture. A sightseeing tour includes Three Powers Square, the National Congress, government buildings and the cathedral, one of Oscar Niemeyer's most recognizable designs in the city.

Brasília makes a worthwhile city stop if your journey through Brazil aims to show not only Rio, colonial towns and natural regions, but also the architectural vision behind the modern capital.

Braulio Carrillo National Park protects dense evergreen forests in Costa Rica's mountains. Its territory spans several elevation zones, so vegetation ranges from humid tropical rainforest to cooler mountain environments. Even the road between San José and the country's Caribbean side reveals this changing scenery.

The park has separate sectors with walking trails for exploring its natural surroundings, including Quebrada González and the area around Barva Volcano. The forest offers a rich diversity of plants and opportunities for birdwatching. Braulio Carrillo reveals Costa Rica's mountainous side and often appears on routes toward the waterways of Tortuguero.
